key_idea: Because the cost is min(dx^2, dy^2), a transition only needs the best dp value per row and per column of the previous number's tiles, so each tile of the next number costs O(n) instead of O(tiles).
sketch: Group tiles by number; for layer v build bestRow[r] and bestCol[c] as the minimum dp over its tiles, keep only the non-empty rows/columns, then for each tile of layer v+1 take min over rows of bestRow[x]+(x-r)^2 and over columns of bestCol[y]+(y-c)^2. Total work is sum over layers of |layer v+1| * min(2n, 2|layer v|) <= 2.5e8 simple ops, well under 0.2 s locally. Output -1 if any number 1..k has no tile, 0 when k = 1. Use 64-bit for totals.
